# OSL V2 CAD findings

Every geometric constant in this repository, with its evidence.

**Do not edit this file by hand.** It is the verbatim output of
`python tools/cad_findings.py`, which re-derives all of it from the untouched
Onshape export. If the script and this document ever disagree, the script is
right — regenerate with:

```
python tools/cad_findings.py > docs/CAD_FINDINGS.md.new
```

Companion evidence: `python tools/verify_visorigin.py` regenerates
`build/verify/visorigin_AB.png`, and `python tools/render_poses.py` regenerates
`build/verify/poses.png`.

---
OSL V2 CAD findings, re-derived from
  osl_v2_0_assembly/urdf/osl_v2_0_assembly.urdf

## Export size and joint mix
links 682   joints 681   {'fixed': 618, 'prismatic': 24, 'continuous': 39}
file  14584 lines

## Why the inertials are unusable
657 inertial blocks, total mass 14.7534 g
  52 have a non-positive eigenvalue (Onshape assigned no
    materials, so every tensor is scaled by an absurd mass)
  8 of those also violate the triangle inequality A + B >= C
  0 non-singular tensors violate it
MuJoCo eigen-decomposes each of these while PARSING, so no compiler
option can rescue them -- hence native MJCF emission.

## Anterior is -X (settled by the foot, not by the battery)
Variflex blade world bbox  x [-0.1665, +0.0756]  y [-0.0331, +0.0313]  z [-0.2302, -0.1737]
  mount hardware z_m8_16mm_socket_mcmaster_96144a216: x=+0.0349 y=-0.0115
  mount hardware z_m8_16mm_socket_mcmaster_96144a216_1: x=+0.0348 y=+0.0108
  mount hardware z_m8_washer_mcmaster_90965a190: x=+0.0352 y=-0.0115
  mount hardware z_m8_washer_mcmaster_90965a190_1: x=+0.0351 y=+0.0108
The blade runs much further from the bolts toward -X than +X, so the
long forefoot is -X and the short heel is +X.

## The Ossur Variflex mate is inherited, not reconstructed
sole lowest z -0.2302 m -> ankle sits 91.5 mm above the sole
lowest point of the whole model -0.2302 m
_check_foot() re-runs the mate test on every build; see its output above.

## The sole is 2.4 deg toe-down at ankle = 0, so the leg cannot stand flat
Lower convex hull of the blade in the sagittal plane, foot body frame
(origin = ankle axis).  This is the only part of the sole a floor can
touch, so it is what decides the standing pose.
  longest lower-hull edge  149.5 mm
    from  x=-0.08936  z=-0.09146   (distal tip, heel blade)
    to    x=+0.06001  z=-0.08521   (heel pad)
  slope +2.3971 deg -> flat-foot ankle angle +2.3971 deg
  ground-scene base height, qpos=0 0.2322 m, flat pose 0.2284 m
The models/*.xml <keyframe name="flat"> holds this pose.  At ankle = 0
the leg balances on the forefoot keel instead, which is why commanding
the ankle used to tip it over.
  at that angle the contact is a patch, not a knife edge:
    173 blade vertices within 2 mm of the lowest point, spanning 161.3 x 64.0 mm
    flat to 0.49 mm rms about a best-fit plane
    residual tilt: sagittal +0.29 deg, frontal +0.00 deg -- the
      frontal term is what a single ankle hinge could NOT have fixed,
      so the pose only works because it comes out at zero
  the rms figure is load-bearing elsewhere: build_mjcf.PENETRATION_LIMIT
  is 0.50 mm, chosen as roughly that rms rather than from any formula,
  because a sole that sinks less than its own unevenness is not the reason
  a stance looks wrong.  check_model.py measures the real depth against it.

## Collision geometry: the blade mesh, plus one bounding box per module
The sole is a type="mesh" geom on the blade itself, so the toe spring
and heel roll-off are exact (both convex).  Everything above the ankle
gets an axis-aligned BOUNDING box whose only job is to keep the leg out
of the floor -- the fill fractions say plainly that these are not shape
claims:
  knee_prox knee_prox_shell [ 78.2  79.  106. ] mm   28 parts   20.7 % full
  shank knee_module   [128.1 118.9 203.8] mm   80 parts   22.2 % full
  shank mid_pylon     [ 65.8 102.4  69.2] mm   11 parts   11.2 % full
  shank ankle_module  [136.5 118.4 192.2] mm   51 parts   19.8 % full
  swept 26x26 = 676 poses over knee -5..+120 deg x ankle -30..+20 deg:
    all 216 visual meshes stay 5.9 mm clear of the lowest collision geom
      worst at knee +95.0 deg, ankle -30.0 deg, binding pair
        ba30_p002_v04_chassis_step_1
        vs the knee_module geom
    the 46 meshes no box contains stay 23.6 mm clear
      worst at knee -5.0 deg, ankle -2.0 deg, binding pair
        z_m8_16mm_socket_mcmaster_96144a216
        vs the sole geom
    the first figure is the smaller of the two because a part inside a box
    on its own body can never rise above it -- that clearance measures how
    close a rotating box corner passes to the part that defined the box,
    not whether anything is exposed.  The second is the real margin.
    Either way nothing can reach the floor before a collision geom does.
    scripts/check_model.py re-derives both from MuJoCo's own forward
    kinematics and fails if either disagrees by more than 0.1 mm.
